sources.entry: Frigate - Monitor your security cameras with locally processed AI. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Python/Nodejs
Frigate | NVR with real-time AI object detection for IP cameras

summary.one_liner: Frigate is a self-hosted network video recorder (NVR) that runs AI object detection locally on feeds from IP cameras, designed to integrate with Home Assistant.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a local NVR that uses OpenCV and TensorFlow to run realtime object detection on IP camera streams, with a GPU or AI accelerator strongly recommended. It uses a low-overhead motion detector to decide where object detection runs, and runs TensorFlow detection in separate processes. Recording supports 24/7 capture and retention settings based on detected objects. It can re-stream camera feeds via RTSP to reduce camera connections, and offers WebRTC and MSE for low-latency live view. Integration is through a custom Home Assistant component and MQTT messaging. The README also names a built-in mask and zone editor and a review workflow with multi-camera scrubbing. Full documentation lives on an external site.
use_cases: record camera footage with object-based retention
run AI person or object detection on camera feeds
re-stream RTSP camera feeds to reduce connections
send camera events over MQTT to other systems
notable: Object detection runs locally with no cloud dependency, per the README
Motion detection gates object detection so only relevant regions are analyzed
Supports GPU and AI accelerator object detectors
Built-in mask and zone editor and review workflow with multi-camera scrubbing
Live view via WebRTC and MSE, plus RTSP re-streaming
caveats: A GPU or AI accelerator is highly recommended for good performance
Tight integration is aimed at Home Assistant users
Full documentation is hosted externally and not in the README
